actors.responsibility: Issue signed satellite-to-domain authority assignments and monotonically allocate AssignmentGeneration and AuthorityIncarnationId.
Authenticate requests, bind idempotency keys, and reject stale client projections before command persistence.
Own the Satellite Control Domain lifecycle and enforce the current authority fence.
Acquire or observe leadership and monotonically advance LeaderEpoch within the current signed satellite assignment.
Validate admission policy and commit resource reservations.
Apply execution transitions, own checkpoints, and isolate workers.
Interpret approved IR and propose safe-point, wait, prompt, and operation events; it cannot commit authoritative state.
Validate controller leases and settle internal control commands.
Hold the sole domain control lease and request authorized execution mutations or prompt settlements.

Use a non-control workspace while separately eligible for Controller capability; may submit, withdraw, decline, or acknowledge one named handover request but has no execution authority until atomic transfer commits.
Observe projections only; this actor is never authorized on a mutating transition.
Change source through the Git workflow only; this actor is never authorized to mutate an active execution by edit action.
Reconcile committed state, checkpoints, commands, prompts, and driver journals after interruption.
Fence and journal typed effect requests and prepare them for final authorization; it has no satellite or GCS effect credential or direct effect egress.
Resolve typed adapter behavior and return bounded evidence through the Effect Authorization Point; it has no direct satellite or GCS effect credential or bypass egress.

Own the sole external-effect credential and egress; hold PostgreSQL final-guard locks, linearly consume the SAA one-use attempt permit, commit the local permit and SAA receipt before send, and fail closed without claiming distributed ACID.

identity_fences.name: AuthorityIncarnationId
identity_fences.rule: Allocated only by the Satellite Assignment Authority for one signed assignment; a replacement never reuses it.

identity_fences.name: AssignmentGeneration
identity_fences.rule: Monotonic per satellite assignment; every mutation and final effect check must match the current signed domain, satellite, authority-incarnation, and assignment-generation tuple.

identity_fences.name: LeaderEpoch
identity_fences.rule: Monotonic per domain; every authoritative mutation must match the current value.

identity_fences.name: ControlFencingToken
identity_fences.rule: Monotonic per domain control grant; every controller mutation must match an unexpired lease.

identity_fences.name: ControllerLeaseId
identity_fences.rule: Unique for one controller grant. Renewal and cancelled handover retain it; acquisition, accepted handover, forced takeover, or reacquisition allocates a new value.

identity_fences.name: ControlLeaseRevision
identity_fences.rule: Monotonic within one control-lease record; acquisition, renewal, release, expiry, revocation, and handover compare-and-set this revision without decreasing or reusing the control fence.

identity_fences.name: ClientInstanceProof
identity_fences.rule: Session-bound proof of possession for a non-exportable client-instance key; interactive mutations must verify it and cannot replay it from another tab, device, server, or request context.

identity_fences.name: ExecutionId
identity_fences.rule: Immutable for one run; terminal executions are never reused by reload, recovery, or rerun.

identity_fences.name: ExecutionRevision
identity_fences.rule: Incremented by each committed execution transition and checked by compare-and-set.

identity_fences.name: CommandId
identity_fences.rule: Unique for one internal control request; an idempotency-key replay returns the same command.

identity_fences.name: PromptId
identity_fences.rule: Unique for one durable prompt; PromptRevision protects the sole settlement.

identity_fences.name: OperationId
identity_fences.rule: Stable across transport retry, reconciliation, and every authorized NO_EFFECT retry; RequestDigest remains unchanged and a retry never allocates a substitute OperationId.

identity_fences.name: AttemptId
identity_fences.rule: Opaque, globally unique, and immutable for one attempt; each accepted AttemptId owns one immutable authority, generation, leader, controller, driver, and execution fence tuple, and an authorized retry allocates a new AttemptId.

identity_fences.name: DriverHostGeneration
identity_fences.rule: Changes at every host start and fences every response from an older host.

identity_fences.name: ContextGeneration
identity_fences.rule: Identifies one immutable opened context configuration.

identity_fences.name: ExecutionAttachmentGeneration
identity_fences.rule: Identifies one immutable execution attachment and changes for a replacement run or approved reload.

identity_fences.name: DriverBindingId
identity_fences.rule: Binds exact host, context, and execution-attachment generations.

safe_points.rule: No statement side effect has begun.
The statement is complete and has no unresolved external operation.
The wait registration or settlement and its consumed evidence are committed.
Prompt open or settlement and the execution transition are durably correlated.
The operation is settled and its effect certainty is recorded.
All required child outcomes and data transfers are committed.
A cleanup hook result is committed; continuation is only to the next cleanup or terminal disposition.

definitions.NO_EFFECT: Authoritative evidence proves that no external effect occurred.
definitions.EFFECT_CONFIRMED: Authoritative evidence proves that the defined external effect occurred.
definitions.EFFECT_POSSIBLE: Dispatch authorization, the SAA receipt, and the local permit commit are durable before send; the effect boundary may have been crossed and the external effect may have occurred.
definitions.EFFECT_UNKNOWN: Available evidence is missing, contradictory, or fails integrity validation.

effect_certainty.retry_rule: Automatic or operator-requested resend is forbidden unless certainty is authoritatively NO_EFFECT, the capability policy permits retry, OperationId and RequestDigest are retained, AttemptNumber increments, a new opaque AttemptId plus new EffectPermitId and SaaAttemptPermitId are allocated, and the new attempt is bound to the then-current fence tuple without rewriting prior-attempt history.

effect_authorization_point.local_authority: current writable primary PostgreSQL control database with required synchronous quorum
effect_authorization_point.saa_authority: Satellite Assignment Authority linearizable one-use attempt-permit service
effect_authorization_point.local_permit_identity: EffectPermitId bound one-to-one to OperationId plus AttemptId, RequestDigest, SaaAttemptPermitId, and that attempt's complete immutable accepted authority and fence tuple
effect_authorization_point.saa_attempt_permit_identity: SaaAttemptPermitId bound one-to-one to the current effect_enabled SAA grant, OperationId, AttemptId, RequestDigest, EffectClass, AssignmentGeneration, AuthorityIncarnationId, and DispatchAuthorityId

ordered_protocol.rule: Begin one primary-PostgreSQL transaction, lock the current local assignment projection, leader, controller-lease pointer and grant, driver binding, execution, operation, and EffectPermitId rows, then validate every local final guard while those locks are held.

While the local transaction and locks remain open, ask SAA to atomically consume the unconsumed SaaAttemptPermitId against the current effect_enabled grant. SAA serializes this decision with assignment revocation and returns a unique signed consume receipt only to the winner.

After a successful SAA consume, persist SaaPermitConsumeReceiptDigest, change EffectPermitId from PENDING to CONSUMED, persist the complete accepted and current fence evidence, set Stage to DISPATCHED and EffectCertainty to EFFECT_POSSIBLE, and commit the local transaction before any send.
Only after the local commit is confirmed may the prepared request leave through the Effect Authorization Point sole effect credential and egress.

serialization.local: Lease release, expiry, revocation, handover, takeover, and effect authorization serialize through the same PostgreSQL rows and locks. If a lease-changing transaction commits first, EAP validation rejects; if the EAP local commit wins, a later lease change cannot erase the already authorized in-flight attempt.
serialization.saa: SaaAttemptPermitId consumption and assignment revocation serialize at SAA. If revocation wins, consume rejects; if consume wins, the receipt remains valid for that one attempt and later revocation blocks future permits without erasing the consumed authorization.
serialization.no_distributed_acid: PostgreSQL and SAA are independent authorities. This protocol is deliberately ordered and recoverable; it does not claim or require a distributed ACID transaction.

final_guard: Satellite Assignment Authority is online and the one-use SaaAttemptPermitId is unconsumed and bound to the current effect_enabled grant with the same AssignmentGeneration, AuthorityIncarnationId, SatelliteId, DomainId, and fresh DispatchAuthorityId recorded in the current attempt's immutable accepted tuple
the locked local domain state is ACTIVE or explicitly effect-capable DEGRADED under the current DegradationPolicyRevision; STANDBY, DRAINING, STOPPED, and FAILED never authorize an external effect
the current elected LeaderEpoch and leader identity match the current attempt's immutable accepted tuple

for interactive effects, the ControllerLeaseId in the current attempt's immutable accepted tuple remains ACTIVE and unexpired with the same holder subject, session, client key, and ControlFencingToken and a valid request ClientInstanceProof
DriverHostGeneration, ContextGeneration, ExecutionAttachmentGeneration, DriverBindingId, ExecutionId, and ExecutionRevision match the current attempt's immutable accepted tuple
EffectPermitId is PENDING, unexpired, unused, and bound to the same OperationId, AttemptId, SaaAttemptPermitId, RequestDigest, and EffectClass
the primary database is writable with required quorum and every assignment, authority, lease, clock, and driver observation meets its freshness bound

failure_outcomes.saa_consume_failed: Roll back the local transaction, retain NO_EFFECT, and do not send.
failure_outcomes.saa_consume_succeeded_local_commit_faile: Do not send. The consumed SaaAttemptPermitId and its receipt are abandoned permanently and never reused; recovery reconciles the attempt from SAA and local evidence before any new attempt is admitted.
failure_outcomes.local_commit_succeeded: The attempt is durably EFFECT_POSSIBLE before send. Later SAA revocation or lease loss cannot erase that in-flight attempt and cannot justify resend.
failure_outcomes.crash_after_local_commit: Recover as EFFECT_POSSIBLE and reconcile by stable operation, attempt, local permit, SAA receipt, and external evidence; never infer NO_EFFECT or resend.

effect_authorization_point.credential_rule: Only EFFECT_AUTHORIZATION_POINT holds the satellite or GCS effect credential and effect-capable network route; browser, worker, gateway, and driver host paths cannot bypass it.
effect_authorization_point.failure_rule: Quorum loss, primary uncertainty, stale or unavailable assignment authority, clock uncertainty, stale fence, expired permit, integrity failure, or egress ownership uncertainty rejects before effect and suspends the owning execution when control or effect certainty cannot be proved.

restart_registry.algorithm: Fence the prior owner, find a target event by CommandId, settle when committed, requeue the same CommandId only when no application occurred and every original guard remains valid, otherwise supersede or retain RECONCILING.
restart_registry.time_rule: Preserve original acceptance, safe-point, and application deadlines from database time.
restart_registry.idempotency_rule: Never allocate a replacement CommandId for retry or recovery.

restart_registry.algorithm: Reconcile the single settlement compare-and-set, republish the same OPEN PromptId when unsettled, and return the winning immutable settlement when settled.
restart_registry.time_rule: Use the original database deadline and no-controller grace; restart never extends either.
restart_registry.idempotency_rule: Response, timeout, cancellation, and termination race for one SettlementId and exactly one winner.

restart_registry.algorithm: Reconcile the owning execution, scheduler decision, attachment hooks, and associated operation dispositions; retain or reacquire no capacity by inference and release only after the owning work has a durable disposition.
restart_registry.time_rule: Preserve original queue and reservation deadlines and starvation-order evidence.
restart_registry.idempotency_rule: Reservation acquisition and release compare-and-set ReservationRevision and never double-count capacity.

restart_registry.algorithm: Discard an uncommitted proposal, validate the latest committed checkpoint against the pinned runtime and configuration, then replay only committed events after its sequence; never cross an unresolved external effect.
restart_registry.time_rule: Preserve every wait, prompt, schedule, and operation target embedded in the checkpoint.
restart_registry.idempotency_rule: CheckpointSequence is monotonic per ExecutionId and a duplicate digest returns the committed checkpoint.

restart_registry.algorithm: Recompute due status from OriginalTarget using the same authoritative clock and uncertainty policy, derive stable OccurrenceId from ScheduleId plus scheduled target, claim it by compare-and-set, and submit at most the bounded policy result through normal admission and effect authorization.
restart_registry.time_rule: Never replace OriginalTarget with restart time; CATCH_UP_BOUNDED cannot exceed MaximumCatchUpOccurrences and coalesces or leaves later occurrences according to the pinned policy.
restart_registry.idempotency_rule: Each OccurrenceId has one idempotency key and can produce at most one admitted execution or effect intent.
restart_registry.failure_rule: Do not claim or fire while clock uncertainty exceeds policy, the Satellite Assignment Authority or leader is unavailable or stale, or the prior occurrence outcome is unresolved.

restart_registry.algorithm: Fence the prior owner, reconcile the same OperationId and AttemptId against the local permit, SAA one-use permit and consume receipt, gateway, driver, Effect Authorization Point, and external evidence, and never resend unless authoritative evidence sets EffectCertainty to NO_EFFECT.
restart_registry.time_rule: Preserve the original operation deadline, attempt history, and reconciliation deadline.
restart_registry.idempotency_rule: A retry retains OperationId and RequestDigest, increments AttemptNumber, and allocates a new AttemptId, EffectPermitId, and SaaAttemptPermitId only after NO_EFFECT proof; a successor OperationId is new intent.

global_invariants: No enum in this model contains CONTROL_HOLD; control loss is execution state SUSPENDED with hold_reason CONTROL_LOST and saved_resume_target.
A state marked terminal has no outgoing transition and cannot reactivate.

An AuthorityIncarnationId enters ACTIVE at most once; authority loss ends FAILED and planned deactivation ends STOPPED, so later activation requires a fresh SAA assignment generation, authority incarnation, and dispatch authority.
A reload, rerun, or recovery requested after FINISHED, ABORTED, or ERROR creates a new ExecutionId and links predecessor_execution_id.

Every mutation validates the current signed satellite assignment and matches AssignmentGeneration, AuthorityIncarnationId, and LeaderEpoch; controller mutations also match ControlLeaseRevision, an unexpired ControlFencingToken, and ClientInstanceProof.
Every entity mutation is a revision compare-and-set and is committed with audit and outbox evidence before publication.
At most one current ControllerLeaseId in ACTIVE or HANDOVER_PENDING exists per DomainId and AuthorityIncarnationId; terminal lease records remain immutable history.
Every new controller grant allocates a new ControllerLeaseId and strictly increases ControlFencingToken; renewal changes only ControlLeaseRevision and expiry.

Final external-effect validation reads the current lease and does not require current ControlLeaseRevision to equal the revision accepted with the command; it requires the same ControllerLeaseId, ACTIVE state, unexpired database-time lease, same holder session and client key, current ControlFencingToken and AuthorityIncarnationId, and a valid request ClientInstanceProof, while retaining both revisions as evidence.
A stale authority, controller, host, context, attachment, binding, execution, command, prompt, or operation generation is rejected before effect.
A checkpoint never crosses an operation in EFFECT_POSSIBLE or EFFECT_UNKNOWN.
EffectCertainty exists only for EffectClass values other than NONE; typed read-only NONE requests omit certainty and never enter the external effect operation machine.

Every external effect requires an EAP protocol that holds PostgreSQL authority, lease, operation, and permit locks; linearly consumes one SAA attempt permit for the current effect_enabled grant; commits the local permit plus SAA receipt and EFFECT_POSSIBLE before send; and uses the sole effect credential and egress without claiming distributed ACID.

Entering DRAINING requires a linearly committed SAA state with effect_enabled false before the local domain transition; DRAINING cannot consume an SAA attempt permit or authorize a new external effect.
Cleanup runs in reverse registered order, continues after individual failure, records every result, and performs configuration cleanup last.
MONITOR and EDITOR cannot appear as actors on a mutating transition.

invariants: ACTIVE or DEGRADED commits require the current signed assignment, AssignmentGeneration, AuthorityIncarnationId, and LeaderEpoch.
Only one AuthorityIncarnationId can commit within one LeaderEpoch.
DOM-003 is the only entry into ACTIVE from outside the ACTIVE-DEGRADED envelope and can commit only once for an AuthorityIncarnationId.
An incarnation that leaves ACTIVE or DEGRADED through authority loss becomes terminal FAILED and cannot return to STANDBY or ACTIVE.
A planned DRAINING deactivation ends terminal STOPPED and never returns the same incarnation to STANDBY.
DRAINING requires signed SAA effect_enabled false, permits settlement and reconciliation only, and cannot authorize or consume a new effect permit.
STANDBY never accepts a mutation or dispatches an operation.

domain_projection.AVAILABLE: No current unexpired ControllerLeaseId in ACTIVE or HANDOVER_PENDING exists for DomainId plus AuthorityIncarnationId. AVAILABLE is a derived domain projection, not a ControllerLeaseGrant state.
domain_projection.singleton_rule: The domain current-lease pointer and grant creation or replacement commit atomically; only its referenced grant can authorize control.

handover_request_contract.singleton_rule: At most one REQUESTED or HOLDER_APPROVED handover request may exist for the domain current-lease pointer; request creation does not change the ACTIVE holder or grant execution authority.
handover_request_contract.ordering_rule: The current holder approves the exact request before the named requester may submit a request-bound responsibility acknowledgement; acknowledgement and transfer commit atomically.
handover_request_contract.mode_rule: The transfer transaction commits authoritative Execution Mode and permitted former-holder non-control projections plus outbox rows; the relay publishes them only after commit, and browser receipt is not the authority boundary.
handover_request_contract.audit_rule: Every source event records trusted database event time, both human identity/session/client-key bindings where applicable, policy revision, reason, outcome, request and correlation IDs, and old/new lease revision and fence evidence. An independent sink receipt records ingestion time and binds the source event ID and digest.

mutation_authentication.human_rule: Every human-initiated lease or handover-request mutation validates the current signed assignment and AuthorityIncarnationId, the exact expected ControlLeaseRevision at acceptance, the actor's authorized session and mode-specific capability, and a request-bound ClientInstanceProof from that actor's non-exportable key; requester proof never substitutes for current-holder approval proof.
mutation_authentication.service_rule: CLOCK, identity, assignment, and authority events use mutually authenticated service evidence, current assignment and authority fences, and database time; they cannot impersonate a holder proof.
mutation_authentication.database_time_rule: Issue, renewal, handover request, holder approval, responsibility acknowledgement, release, expiry, revocation, and replacement decisions use database time only.

effect_boundary_guard.acceptance: Command acceptance checks exact expected ControlLeaseRevision and records accepted_control_lease_revision.
effect_boundary_guard.final_effect: Immediately before an external effect, EFFECT_AUTHORIZATION_POINT holds the PostgreSQL authority, lease, operation, and local-permit locks; validates the same ControllerLeaseId in ACTIVE state before ExpiresAtDatabaseTime with the same holder, session, client key, fence, assignment, authority, and request proof; linearly consumes the SAA one-use attempt permit for the current effect_enabled grant; then commits the local permit and SAA receipt before send.
effect_boundary_guard.renewal_nuance: Final effect validation does not require current ControlLeaseRevision to equal accepted_control_lease_revision because a benign renewal or non-authorizing handover-request metadata transition may advance it without changing the ACTIVE holder or fence. Holder approval changes state to HANDOVER_PENDING and therefore rejects effect. Record current_control_lease_revision with accepted_control_lease_revision as effect evidence.
effect_boundary_guard.failure: A failed SAA consume rolls back the local transaction. A successful SAA consume followed by local commit failure sends nothing and permanently abandons that SAA permit. A successful local commit makes the attempt EFFECT_POSSIBLE before send. PostgreSQL and SAA serialize changes independently; this is not distributed ACID.

states.name: HANDOVER_PENDING
states.description: The current holder approved one named request and the requester must acknowledge responsibility before the deadline; no new external effect is authorized while this state is current.

states.name: RELEASED

states.name: EXPIRED

states.name: REVOKED
states.description: Administrative, identity, assignment, authority, or integrity policy terminated this grant.

states.name: TRANSFERRED

invariants: This machine accepts only EffectClass values other than NONE; read-only NONE requests never carry EffectCertainty.
Stage and effect_certainty are orthogonal fields and must never be inferred from each other.
The certainty enum is exactly NO_EFFECT, EFFECT_CONFIRMED, EFFECT_POSSIBLE, EFFECT_UNKNOWN.
A transport timeout or cancellation is not proof of NO_EFFECT.
No resend occurs from EFFECT_POSSIBLE or EFFECT_UNKNOWN.

A retry after authoritative NO_EFFECT retains OperationId and RequestDigest, preserves prior-attempt history unchanged, increments AttemptNumber, allocates a new opaque AttemptId, EffectPermitId, and SaaAttemptPermitId, and binds the new attempt to the then-current authority and fence tuple, which may differ from the prior attempt's tuple.

Every accepted AttemptId has exactly one immutable authority, generation, leader, controller, driver, and execution fence tuple; no retry rewrites a prior tuple or treats it as current without fresh validation.
SAA permit consumption and the local PostgreSQL commit are ordered independent authority decisions, not a distributed ACID transaction.
A failed SAA consume rolls back locally; a successful SAA consume followed by local commit failure sends nothing and permanently abandons that SaaAttemptPermitId.
A successful local permit and SAA receipt commit establishes EFFECT_POSSIBLE before send, and later authority or lease loss cannot erase the in-flight attempt.
A successor OperationId represents new intent and is never described as retry of a prior OperationId.
SETTLED never reactivates; later corrective operator intent is a new operation with an explicit relationship.
An authorized unresolved disposition does not upgrade or erase effect certainty.
